critical_issues: MEASUREMENT-BOUNDARY UNVERIFIED (the single most dangerous hole): the spec ASSERTS that llama.cpp test-backend-ops `perf` reports 'per-op GPU time' comparable to AXIOM's GpuTimestamp TOP_OF_PIPE->BOTTOM_OF_PIPE span, but does NOT establish HOW test-backend-ops actually measures. Historically test-backend-ops `perf` times a loop of op evaluations with CPU-side timing around a batched run (ggml_backend_graph_compute over many repetitions) and divides — it does NOT necessarily use GPU timestamp queries per op. If llama.cpp's number is CPU-wall-over-N-runs while AXIOM's is a pure on-device timestamp span, the two boundaries DIFFER: AXIOM excludes submit/scheduling per dispatch (MIN-of-10 of pure GPU span) while llama.cpp amortizes submit across many runs but still includes its own command-buffer/queue overhead. The spec must REQUIRE the Coder to read test-backend-ops.cpp at the pinned SHA and document, verbatim in ab_results.json, exactly what its timer brackets (GPU timestamp vs CPU wall, per-op vs batched-amortized). Without that, the ratio is not provably apples-to-apples in EITHER direction. Note AXIOM uses MIN-of-10 while llama.cpp perf typically reports a MEAN/throughput over its run loop — min-vs-mean is itself a boundary mismatch that flatters AXIOM and must be disclosed.

GEMV (n=1) EXISTENCE IN test-backend-ops IS UNVERIFIED. The entire PRIMARY kill-criterion comparison (AXIOM matvec vs llama.cpp GEMV) presumes test-backend-ops perf enumerates a MUL_MAT Q4_K case with n==1. The spec itself lists this as an open question (open_questions[4]) yet builds the headline number on it. If the only registered Q4_K MUL_MAT cases are GEMM-shaped (n in {8,16,512,...}), the fail-closed path 'pick the closest K and label' would silently turn the kill-criterion number into an AXIOM-matvec-vs-llama-GEMM comparison — exactly the apples-to-oranges trap, and one that makes AXIOM look ARTIFICIALLY WORSE (GEMM amortizes weight load over n columns; comparing per-output throughput is unfair to AXIOM, but if the harness normalizes by n it becomes unfair to llama.cpp). The spec MUST add a HARD RULE: if no n==1 Q4_K MUL_MAT case exists, the kill-criterion is marked INCOMPLETE (not a FAIL number) and a custom test-backend-ops invocation or a n=1 case is added — NEVER substitute a GEMM ratio as 'the kill-criterion number.'
warnings: FLOP-CONVENTION MISMATCH RISK: the spec computes TFLOPS = 2*M*N*K on both sides and 'recomputes us from GFLOPS and m/n/k' for llama.cpp. But it must EXPLICITLY assert that llama.cpp's reported GFLOPS for Q4_K counts ONLY the 2*M*N*K matmul MACs and NOT the dequant ALU (which is substantial for Q4_K). AXIOM's q4km kernel does far more dequant work per output than 2*K FLOPs, yet the spec counts AXIOM at 2*1*K too. As long as BOTH count 2*M*N*K matmul-only, the ratio is consistent — but the spec must STATE that AXIOM's reported TFLOPS is matmul-equivalent-FLOPs (dequant excluded), so a reader does not mistake it for total ALU throughput. Currently this is implicit.

MIN-of-10 (AXIOM) vs throughput-over-run-loop (llama.cpp) is a statistic mismatch. AXIOM reports the single fastest dispatch; llama.cpp perf reports an averaged/sustained throughput. Best-case-vs-sustained slightly flatters AXIOM. Disclose explicitly; ideally report AXIOM median too for context.

STALE/WRONG existing resident bench is the justification but is mis-described. The spec says 'the existing resident q4km bench uses all-zero dummy weights.' VERIFIED: resident_matmul.rs `resident_timing_kernels/q4km_matvec` (lines 214-217) uses BOTH all-zero weights AND a WRONG block_size_bytes=64 ('Q4_K_M block is 64 bytes (simplified)') when the real superblock is 144 bytes — so that bench dispatches a kernel reading past/under its real layout with garbage dims. The new A/B bench correctly uses 144-byte real superblocks via generate_q4km_test_data. GOOD, but the spec should note the existing bench is doubly-broken (zeros + wrong 64B size) so QA does not treat the existing bench's number as any kind of baseline.

LLAMACPP PIN must be a recorded SHA, not a floating tag. The spec waffles ('pin to the latest master tag... e.g. a b#### release tag... RECORD the SHA'). Make it unambiguous: the script's LLAMACPP_COMMIT default is a literal 40-char SHA committed into the script and ab_results.json; tags are resolved to that SHA once and frozen. A tag can be re-pointed; only a SHA is reproducible.

DEVICE-MATCH ASSERTION wording is soft: 'assert ... contains RTX PRO 6000 (or record if it differs) and FAIL LOUDLY if the two sides ran on different devices.' The 'or record if it differs' clause is an escape hatch that could let a mismatched run produce a number. Make it: FAIL CLOSED if the two device strings are not byte-identical, regardless of model name; the 'RTX PRO 6000' substring check is secondary.
vendor_concerns: AMD/Intel halves deferred to EB.1 hardware. ACCEPTED as honest scope: DESIGN §5 kill criterion is 'within 15% on ANY vendor,' so a NVIDIA FAIL with the current single-row kernel does NOT trip the kill criterion (AMD/Intel pending). The spec frames this correctly. Confirm ROADMAP marks AMD/Intel 'deferred-not-dropped' and BENCHMARKS does not imply the kill criterion is decided.

The kill criterion in DESIGN §5 is attached to the M2 SLIP GATE (within 15% on any vendor), not an M3 gate. M3.4 runs that comparison early on NVIDIA as a baseline. The spec should make explicit that an NVIDIA FAIL here is a pre-M2-gate data point, not the firing of the kill criterion (which is evaluated 'on any vendor' across AMD/Intel too). Avoid any prose that reads as 'kill criterion FAILED' without the 'on NVIDIA only, other vendors pending, criterion is any-vendor' qualifier.
missing_tests: MUST DOCUMENT (in ab_results.json, machine-readable): the exact test-backend-ops timing mechanism at the pinned SHA (GPU-timestamp vs CPU-wall; per-op vs batched-amortized; mean vs min). Without this the AT-1760 artifact cannot be audited for boundary comparability.

MUST TEST/ASSERT: that the selected llama.cpp line is n==1 (GEMV) for the kill-criterion number; if not present, AT-1762 must record kill_criterion status=INCOMPLETE, NOT a FAIL ratio computed against a GEMM case.

MUST ASSERT: llama.cpp parsed m/n/k yields the SAME 2*M*N*K FLOP count the harness uses to recompute us; reject the line if GFLOPS and recomputed-from-m/n/k us are inconsistent beyond a tolerance (guards against a FLOP-convention drift, e.g. llama.cpp counting 2x for FMA or including dequant).
questions_for_architect: At the pinned SHA, does test-backend-ops `perf` bracket each op with GPU timestamp queries, or with CPU wall-clock around a batched repetition loop? (Determines whether AXIOM-GpuTimestamp vs llama.cpp is boundary-comparable.)
Does test-backend-ops perf enumerate a Q4_K MUL_MAT case with n==1? If not, what is the EXACT fallback — and do you agree it must be INCOMPLETE, never a GEMM-substituted FAIL number?
Is AXIOM's MIN-of-10 compared against llama.cpp's mean/sustained throughput? If so, will you also report AXIOM's median and llama.cpp's best-case (if available) so the statistic is symmetric?
Will the pin be a literal 40-char SHA frozen in the script + ab_results.json (not a re-pointable tag)?
Will the device-match assertion fail-closed on ANY device-string difference (not just absence of 'RTX PRO 6000')?
summary: The methodology is fundamentally HONEST and the framing of an expected NVIDIA loss is commendable — no spin, real weights (correctly fixing the genuine zero-weight + wrong-64-byte-size bug in the existing resident_timing_kernels/q4km_matvec bench), GEMV-vs-matvec as primary with GEMM labeled context-only, same ICD, mechanical verdict, vendor/ gitignored, results committed (verified .pipeline/benchmarks/.gitignore only excludes candidate-baselines.json so m34/ab_results.json WILL land). NEEDS_REVISION on three fairness/reproducibility holes, all fixable in the spec without changing the design: (1) the measurement-boundary between AXIOM's pure on-device GpuTimestamp span (MIN-of-10) and llama.cpp test-backend-ops perf (likely CPU-wall over a batched run loop, reported as sustained throughput) is ASSERTED comparable but NOT established — the Coder must read test-backend-ops.cpp at the pinned SHA and record exactly what its timer brackets; min-vs-mean and per-op-vs-amortized must be disclosed; (2) the n==1 GEMV case the entire kill-criterion number rests on is UNVERIFIED to exist in test-backend-ops — the spec must forbid silently substituting a GEMM ratio and mark INCOMPLETE instead; (3) the FLOP convention (matmul-MACs-only, dequant-excluded) must be asserted identical on both sides via a GFLOPS-vs-recomputed-us consistency check. Also: pin a literal SHA not a tag, and make the device-match assertion fail-closed on any difference. Fix these five and this becomes a fair, honest, reproducible A/B.
